Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors: Left arm numbness with weakness and tingling starting about two weeks ago during boxing; neck pain; transient left-eye vision disturbance (~20 minutes); fatigue; occasional headaches. No known chronic medical conditions reported.  
- Family history of chronic conditions: Father with hypothyroidism and autoimmune issues; mother with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia. No explicit neurological family history documented.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines: Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented); Vitamin D (dose/route/frequency not documented); Iron supplements (taken infrequently; dose/route/frequency not documented); Melatonin (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus): Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks: Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use: Participates in boxing class; reported heavy alcohol use about one month ago; no information provided on tobacco or other substances.  
- Hearing and vision concerns: Transient left-eye visual disturbance lasting ~20 minutes; no ongoing vision issues documented; no glasses or contact lenses reported.  
- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm): Not recorded; patient expressed worry about symptoms.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working diagnosis (provisional): Suspected demyelinating process affecting central nervous system (MS spectrum) with optic pathway involvement and spinal/neuraxial sensory symptoms; urgent neurology evaluation and neuroimaging planned.  
- Key supporting clinical findings from transcript: Transient unilateral (left) vision disturbance; left-arm numbness with weakness and difficulty with fine motor tasks (piano); neck pain; symptoms evolving over about two weeks; boxing-related activity; age range compatible with demyelinating disorders; family history of autoimmune disease.  
- Relevant differentials from DDx that support or refine impression:
  - Multiple sclerosis (MS) with demyelinating manifestations – high likelihood per transcript and DDx rationale; supported by optic symptoms and unilateral limb sensory deficits with subacute evolution.  
  - Transient ischemic attack / amaurosis fugax (vascular etiology) – medium likelihood; unilateral sensory symptoms with transient vision disturbance could reflect vascular causes, though progression over weeks is less typical.  
  - Cervical radiculopathy or cervical spondylotic myelopathy – medium likelihood; neck pain with unilateral arm numbness/weakness; boxing-related strain could contribute.  
- Additional considerations (uncertain options): Neoplasm (brain/spinal) and other inflammatory neuropathies; metabolic neuropathies (e.g., B12 deficiency) also plausible but less well explained by current phrasing.  
- Plan: Proceed with urgent neurology referral and brain imaging (MRI) to evaluate for demyelinating disease or other intracranial/pathway pathology. Instruct patient on red-flag symptoms warranting urgent evaluation (progression to legs, new severe headaches, vomiting, seizures, or worsening visual symptoms) and advise return to urgent care if these occur. No treatment started at this visit pending diagnostic clarification.  
- Conflict noted: None between transcript and DDx.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Multiple sclerosis (MS) with demyelinating manifestations (optic neuritis and limb sensory symptoms)
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Transient monocular vision disturbance and unilateral arm numbness/weakness in a middle-aged adult with episodes over weeks; family autoimmune history; clinician note of MS as a consideration with urgent neurology imaging planned.

- Transient ischemic attack / amaurosis fugax (vascular etiology)
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Unilateral numbness/weakness with transient left-eye vision loss; vascular etiologies can present with such symptoms; however, subacute progression over weeks is less typical for a classic TIA and vascular risk factors were not documented.

- Cervical radiculopathy or cervical spondylotic myelopathy
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Neck pain with left-arm numbness/weakness and sensory changes; could reflect degenerative cervical spine disease; boxing-related strain could contribute; does not fully explain transient vision loss.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note)

- Internal conflicts or contradictions: None identified between transcript and DDx.  
- Transcript quality notes: Conversation provides symptom description but lacks formal physical examination and objective measurements at this visit.

End of note.
